speedsNote: Figure 20's legend: the horizontal speed of the central cluster of each pane, from high-speed film against a 1 ft grid, constant from the window to 5 ft. The text calls the sheets 1/8 and 1/4 in. No glass moved until 0.015 s after the detonation; the 3 mm lines cross zero at about 0.015-0.016 s, the 6 mm at about 0.016 and 0.022 s (read off the figure). A strip about 2 in wide round each edge left slower, rotating, and spread in the plane.

fragments.note: Section 5.2.3 (shot 2's annealed sheet's 4 in edge band; its centre broke into much larger pieces, in bending of the opposite sign) and 8.1 (the tempered sheets held together as clusters of dice, 2-3 in, that penetrated the foam as deeply as annealed glass). About 5% of shot 2's annealed and as-received tempered glass, the sheets weighing about 2.34 kg, was caught in the backstop (129 g and 100 g).
